transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’ve just been feeling really worn out almost every day. It’s like I’ll get what should be a full night’s sleep, but when I wake up, my body still feels heavy and my head feels kind of slow, like I’m already behind before the day even starts. 

I work as a cashier, and when I’m getting up for my shift, I just feel like I’m dragging myself through the morning. It’s not like I’m staying out all night or anything, so it’s been frustrating. I keep thinking I should feel rested, but I don’t.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I’m definitely frustrated and kind of worn down by feeling tired so much, and that can put me in a bad mood, but I haven’t really sat there thinking, like, “I’m depressed,” if that makes sense.

It’s more like… I’m just drained. Some days I’m quieter than usual or I don’t have much energy to deal with people, but I’m not sure if that’s the same thing as feeling down. I guess I’d say not really depressed, more just… tired and annoyed that I can’t seem to shake it.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly when you sleep?

Um… not really, no. I mean, nobody’s said anything to me about it, at least not like “you snore really loud” or anything. I don’t usually have someone watching me sleep, obviously, so I guess I can’t say for sure what I do the whole night, but it hasn’t been something anyone’s brought up.

I’ve wondered about that kind of thing just because I wake up tired, but as far as I know, I’m not known for snoring or anything like that.
Have you been feeling unusually cold compared with other people?

Um… unusually cold? I don’t think so. I mean, I get cold sometimes like anyone else, especially if I’m standing near the doors at work when people keep coming in and out, but I wouldn’t say I’m colder than other people in a way that’s stood out to me.

Like, I haven’t been needing a jacket when everyone else is fine or anything like that. At home I’m pretty normal with the temperature, I think. So… no, I don’t think that’s really been a thing I’ve noticed.
Do you have trouble falling asleep at night?

Yeah… I do. That’s probably one of the bigger things, honestly. I’ll be tired when I get into bed, like my body feels ready to be done for the day, but then as soon as I’m lying there and it’s quiet, my brain kind of turns on.

I start thinking through stuff — bills, whether I forgot to pay something, what my work schedule is going to look like, if I’m going to be too tired at work, things going on at home, whether everyone’s okay. It’s not even always one huge problem, it’s like a bunch of little things lining up and I just keep going over them. And I’ll tell myself, “Okay, stop thinking about it, just sleep,” but that doesn’t really work.

So yeah, most nights it takes me a while to fall asleep. And even when I do finally sleep, it doesn’t feel like I really settled down all the way. I wake up feeling like I never fully rested.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot on most days?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I try not to call it “worrying” all the time because sometimes it feels like I’m just thinking things through, but honestly it’s most days. My mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next and doesn’t really stay quiet.

Like I’ll be thinking about money, then I’ll start thinking about the relative staying with us and whether that’s putting strain on everybody, then I’ll notice my wife seems stressed and I start worrying about her, and then I remember something I said I’d help with at church, and then suddenly I’m thinking about work and whether I messed something up at the register or if people think I’m not doing a good job. It’s like one concern hands off to the next one.

And it’s not always some huge crisis, you know? It’s more like my brain keeps making a list and then checking it over and over. Even if one thing is okay, there’s another thing right behind it. So… yeah, I’d say I worry a lot on most days.
Is it hard for you to stop or control the worrying once it starts?

Yeah… that’s the part that gets me. I can start off with one worry and tell myself, “Okay, just leave it alone,” or I’ll try to pray on it and let it be, because I know sitting there chewing on it isn’t helping anything. But once it starts, it’s like it gets momentum.

I’ll think, “What if I forgot something for work?” and then that turns into, “What if I get in trouble?” and then, “What if that messes up money?” and then I’m thinking about every bad way the whole day could go before it’s even happened. Even if I try to redirect myself, it keeps circling back, or it grabs onto the next thing.

So yeah, I can sometimes calm it down a little, but it’s hard to actually stop it once it gets going.
Has this kind of worrying been going on for 6 months or more?

Yeah… definitely more than six months. I’d say it’s been about a year and three months now, give or take. It really started after our older relative moved in with us. At first I thought it was just an adjustment period, like everybody getting used to a different routine in the house, but it just kind of kept going.

So yeah, it’s not something that only started recently. It’s been over a year at this point.
Do you often feel keyed up or on edge?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t know if I’d call it “keyed up” exactly. I mean, I’m not bouncing off the walls or anything like that. But I do have times where I feel like I’m kind of braced for something, if that makes sense… like I’m waiting for the next thing to need my attention.

It’s not constant, or at least I don’t think it is. Sometimes I only notice it after I’ve already been sitting there tense for a while. But I guess I wouldn’t say I feel relaxed as much as I probably should. I’m just not sure if that’s the same as being on edge.
Do you often notice your muscles feeling tense or tight?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I walk around thinking, “My muscles are tense,” if that makes sense. I’m not someone who pays a lot of attention to my body unless something is really bothering me.

Sometimes I’ll notice my shoulders are kind of up, or my jaw feels a little tight, but I don’t know if that’s a regular thing or just, you know, normal from working or standing around. Like at the register, I’m on my feet and doing the same motions, so it’s hard for me to tell what’s stress and what’s just being tired from the day.

So… I wouldn’t say I often notice it, no. Maybe here and there, but it’s not something I’ve really been tracking.
Do you often have trouble concentrating because your mind is preoccupied with worries?

Yeah, that does happen. Not all day every day, but enough that I notice it, especially at work. Like, I’ll be at the register and I’m literally looking right at the screen, scanning things, taking cash, all of that, and then I realize my mind has kind of gone somewhere else — usually thinking about stuff at home or bills, what needs to be paid, whether something’s going to come up.

And then I lose track of where I was. Sometimes it’s small, like I have to pause and double-check the total or recount the drawer because I don’t trust that I followed it right the first time. Or I’ll catch a small mistake and think, “Okay, I need to focus,” but it’s frustrating because I was trying to focus. It’s like the worry is running in the background and it pulls me away even when I’m doing something pretty straightforward.
Have you been more irritable than usual?

I don’t know that I’d say I’ve been more irritable than usual. I mean, everybody gets annoyed sometimes, especially when work is busy or people are impatient in line, but I haven’t really noticed myself snapping at people or feeling angry all the time.

Maybe I get a little short in my head, if that makes sense — like I’ll feel frustrated faster than I’d like — but I don’t know if that’s actually more than usual or just normal stress. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m being especially irritable or anything. So… I’m not sure. It’s not one of the main things I’ve noticed.
Do you often feel easily fatigued during the day?

Yeah… that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I feel worn out almost every day, and not just like, “Oh, I had a long shift” tired. It’s more like I wake up already dragging, even if I got what should be a full night’s sleep.

I’ll get up for my cashier shift and my body feels heavy, and my head feels kind of slow, like I’m starting the day behind before I’ve even done anything. And then standing at the register all day, talking to people, keeping track of everything — it feels like it takes more out of me than it used to.

So yes, I’d say I do feel easily fatigued during the day. It’s pretty frustrating because I keep thinking sleep should fix it, but a lot of mornings it just doesn’t feel like it does.
Do your worries happen during the day too, or mostly only when you’re trying to fall asleep at night?

It happens during the day too, definitely. It’s not just when I’m lying there trying to fall asleep, though that can be when it gets louder because there’s nothing else going on.

But during the day, my mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next. Like I’ll be at work and start thinking about money — what’s due, what we can cover, what we can’t — and then it shifts to the relative staying with us, and whether that’s putting more pressure on things at home. Then I’ll think about my wife being stressed, and if I’m doing enough to help her, and then somehow it jumps to church stuff I said I’d help with, or whether I forgot something.

And at work it turns into, like, “Am I messing this up? Did I count that right? Did I miss something?” So yeah, it’s kind of all through the day. It’s like my brain doesn’t stay on one worry — it just keeps moving down the list.
Do you often feel restless?

Restless… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who’s pacing around all the time or unable to sit still, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I do feel kind of unsettled, like I can’t fully relax, but I don’t know if I’d call it “restless” exactly. At work I’m standing and moving anyway, so it’s hard to tell. And at home, I might shift around or feel like I should be doing something, but I haven’t really paid attention to it as a separate thing.

So… maybe a little? But I wouldn’t say it’s something I’ve clearly noticed or that stands out to me.
Have these worries been making it hard for you to function day to day?

Yeah… I think they have, though I still get through the day, so sometimes I tell myself it’s not that bad. But it is affecting things.

At work, for example, I’ve been double-checking my cash drawer a lot more than I used to because I’ve made these small mistakes, or I worry that I did. So I’ll count things again, or go back over it in my head, and it slows me down. I don’t think I’m falling apart at work or anything, but it makes the shift feel harder, and I feel less confident doing something I’ve done for a long time.

And outside of work, I’ve cut back on volunteering at the food pantry. I used to help more regularly, and I still care about it, but lately I just feel like I can’t keep up with everything. It’s like adding one more responsibility makes me feel overloaded, even if it’s something good. Then I feel guilty for stepping back, but also relieved because I don’t know if I could handle it on top of everything else.

So yes, day to day I’m functioning, but it’s taking more effort, and I’ve had to pull back from some things.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yeah, it’s definitely not just one thing. If it were only one problem, maybe it would feel easier to pin down, but it’s more like my mind keeps hopping around.

I’ll start out thinking about money — like what bills are coming up, whether we’re stretched too thin — and then before I’ve even settled that in my head, I’m thinking about the relative staying with us and how that affects the house. Then I start worrying about my wife being stressed and whether I’m doing enough or making it worse somehow. And then it’ll jump to church responsibilities, like something I said I’d help with, or whether I forgot to follow through.

And then work gets mixed in too. I’ll be thinking, “Did I mess up? Did I count something wrong? Am I going to make another mistake?” So it’s not really one specific problem. It feels like there’s a whole list, and my brain just keeps moving down it, even when I’m trying to focus on whatever’s actually in front of me.

Or I’ll catch a small mistake and think, “Okay, I need to focus,” but it’s frustrating because I was trying to focus. It’s like the worry is running in the background and it pulls me away even when I’m doing something pretty straightforward.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has another core associated symptom of generalized anxiety disorder—irritability—to help distinguish GAD from primary insomnia, unspecified anxiety, depression, or anemia.
doctor.question: Have you been more irritable than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about irritability, but the provided symptom profile does not include an irritability symptom item.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I’d say I’ve been more irritable than usual. I mean, everybody gets annoyed sometimes, especially when work is busy or people are impatient in line, but I haven’t really noticed myself snapping at people or feeling angry all the time.

Maybe I get a little short in my head, if that makes sense — like I’ll feel frustrated faster than I’d like — but I don’t know if that’s actually more than usual or just normal stress. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m being especially irritable or anything. So… I’m not sure. It’s not one of the main things I’ve noticed.

inference.note: Persistent excessive, difficult-to-control worry for >6 months with insomnia and concentration problems strongly supports F41.1. Current turn does not support depression, and prior history argues against anemia as a primary explanation, so F32.9 and D64.9 are removed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has the additional DSM-5 associated symptom of fatigue/restlessness from generalized anxiety disorder to distinguish GAD from unspecified anxiety disorder and insomnia disorder.
doctor.question: Do you often feel easily fatigued during the day?

target_item.name: Fatigue
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel worn out almost every day, like even after a full night's sleep my body and head are still dragging when I get up for my cashier shift.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about feeling easily fatigued during the day, which matches the fatigue symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I feel worn out almost every day, and not just like, “Oh, I had a long shift” tired. It’s more like I wake up already dragging, even if I got what should be a full night’s sleep.

I’ll get up for my cashier shift and my body feels heavy, and my head feels kind of slow, like I’m starting the day behind before I’ve even done anything. And then standing at the register all day, talking to people, keeping track of everything — it feels like it takes more out of me than it used to.

So yes, I’d say I do feel easily fatigued during the day. It’s pretty frustrating because I keep thinking sleep should fix it, but a lot of mornings it just doesn’t feel like it does.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the worry is generalized across multiple domains rather than confined to sleep, to distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from insomnia disorder or unspecified anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Do your worries happen during the day too, or mostly only when you’re trying to fall asleep at night?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church duties, and whether I'm messing up at work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient’s worries occur during the day as well as at night, which is most directly about the persistence and breadth of excessive worry.

patient.answer:
It happens during the day too, definitely. It’s not just when I’m lying there trying to fall asleep, though that can be when it gets louder because there’s nothing else going on.

But during the day, my mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next. Like I’ll be at work and start thinking about money — what’s due, what we can cover, what we can’t — and then it shifts to the relative staying with us, and whether that’s putting more pressure on things at home. Then I’ll think about my wife being stressed, and if I’m doing enough to help her, and then somehow it jumps to church stuff I said I’d help with, or whether I forgot something.

And at work it turns into, like, “Am I messing this up? Did I count that right? Did I miss something?” So yeah, it’s kind of all through the day. It’s like my brain doesn’t stay on one worry — it just keeps moving down the list.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has restlessness, the remaining key GAD symptom that would help distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from unspecified anxiety disorder and primary insomnia.
doctor.question: Do you often feel restless?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about restlessness, but the provided symptom profile does not include a restlessness symptom item.

patient.answer:
Restless… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who’s pacing around all the time or unable to sit still, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I do feel kind of unsettled, like I can’t fully relax, but I don’t know if I’d call it “restless” exactly. At work I’m standing and moving anyway, so it’s hard to tell. And at home, I might shift around or feel like I should be doing something, but I haven’t really paid attention to it as a separate thing.

So… maybe a little? But I wouldn’t say it’s something I’ve clearly noticed or that stands out to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the anxiety and insomnia are causing clinically significant impairment, which helps distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from unspecified anxiety disorder and primary insomnia.
doctor.question: Have these worries been making it hard for you to function day to day?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've had to double-check my cash drawer more often because of small mistakes, and I've cut back on volunteering at the food pantry because I don't feel like I can keep up with everything.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worries are interfering with day-to-day functioning, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think they have, though I still get through the day, so sometimes I tell myself it’s not that bad. But it is affecting things.

At work, for example, I’ve been double-checking my cash drawer a lot more than I used to because I’ve made these small mistakes, or I worry that I did. So I’ll count things again, or go back over it in my head, and it slows me down. I don’t think I’m falling apart at work or anything, but it makes the shift feel harder, and I feel less confident doing something I’ve done for a long time.

And outside of work, I’ve cut back on volunteering at the food pantry. I used to help more regularly, and I still care about it, but lately I just feel like I can’t keep up with everything. It’s like adding one more responsibility makes me feel overloaded, even if it’s something good. Then I feel guilty for stepping back, but also relieved because I don’t know if I could handle it on top of everything else.

So yes, day to day I’m functioning, but it’s taking more effort, and I’ve had to pull back from some things.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the worry is generalized across multiple domains enough to support generalized anxiety disorder rather than unspecified anxiety or primary insomnia.
doctor.question: Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church duties, and whether I'm messing up at work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worry spans many areas of life rather than one specific problem, which directly matches excessive anxiety and worry about a number of events or activities.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it’s definitely not just one thing. If it were only one problem, maybe it would feel easier to pin down, but it’s more like my mind keeps hopping around.

I’ll start out thinking about money — like what bills are coming up, whether we’re stretched too thin — and then before I’ve even settled that in my head, I’m thinking about the relative staying with us and how that affects the house. Then I start worrying about my wife being stressed and whether I’m doing enough or making it worse somehow. And then it’ll jump to church responsibilities, like something I said I’d help with, or whether I forgot to follow through.

And then work gets mixed in too. I’ll be thinking, “Did I mess up? Did I count something wrong? Am I going to make another mistake?” So it’s not really one specific problem. It feels like there’s a whole list, and my brain just keeps moving down it, even when I’m trying to focus on whatever’s actually in front of me.

inference.note: F41.1 strengthened: excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple domains for >12 months with fatigue, impaired concentration, sleep disturbance, and functional impact. F41.9 is less likely given the symptom pattern now clearly meets criteria for generalized anxiety. G47.00 remains as comorbid insomnia but appears secondary to anxiety.
